main_wing_spar.name: Tapered I-Beam Main Spar
main_wing_spar.model: Timoshenko beam FEA, 2 DOF/node, 21 sizing stations + Saint-Venant root-warping stress recovery
assumptions: Same solver and stations as the contract FeaResult; optimisation scales t_f and t_w linearly root→tip
Gauges clamped to Raymer minimums t_f ≥ 2.0 mm, t_w ≥ 1.5 mm
Mass is one semi-span of spar (multiply by 2 for both wings)
main_wing_spar.convergence_note: Stations fixed by the spar sizing (21 nodes).

metrics.governing: outer cap fibre at y = 0.55 m

ai_proposal.rationale: The spar is nearly critical across the inboard and mid-span cap stations (284-304 MPa), so we modestly trim the lightly loaded tip gauge while slightly reinforcing the root to keep the y = 0.55 m cap bending margin above 0.10.

verified_metrics.governing: outer cap fibre at y = 0.55 m

ai_proposal.verdict: accepted: solver confirms the constraint and a near-optimal objective

ai_proposal.rationale: Shifting mass from the lightly stressed tip toward the inboard root cap reduces the governing bending stress at y = 0.55 m without exceeding baseline mass.

ai_proposal.rationale: Thickening the root cap and web while tapering the outboard tip zone maximizes section modulus at the governing y = 0.55 m station within the 5% mass allowance.

wing_skin_box.name: NACA 2415 Wing Torsion Box
wing_skin_box.model: NACA 2415 single-cell thin-wall box: Timoshenko bending + Bredt-Batho torsion, 25 nodes
assumptions: Skin carries the full ultimate wing bending (spar caps excluded: conservative, no stringers)
Torque t(y) = q·c·(0.10 − 0.05/1.2): lift at c/4, box reference at 0.35c, c_m0 = −0.05 at c_l ≈ 1.2
Spar webs at 15% and 60% chord; 10 ribs per side, 0.8 mm, 50% lightening holes
Uniform-gauge baseline from a first-pass hand sizing to margin +0.25; skin buckling not checked
wing_skin_box.convergence_note: Peak σ_vM re-solved at three node counts.

metrics.governing: skin (bending + Bredt torsion) at y = 0.00 m

ai_proposal.rationale: With a 0.25 baseline margin at the root and rapidly decaying outboard bending and Bredt torsion stresses, both root and tip skin gauges can be reduced while preserving a 0.10 margin.

verified_metrics.governing: skin (bending + Bredt torsion) at y = 0.00 m

ai_proposal.verdict: rejected: feasible but more than 2% worse than the solver grid optimum (41.46 kg vs 39.85 kg)

ai_proposal.rationale: Reallocating skin mass from the lightly loaded outboard torsion box to the governing y = 0.00 m root section lowers peak combined bending and shear stress at constant mass.

horizontal_tail.name: Horizontal Tail NACA 0012 Box
horizontal_tail.model: NACA 0012 single-cell thin-wall box: Timoshenko bending + Bredt-Batho torsion, 21 nodes
assumptions: Tail semi-span 0.357 × wing semi-span and root chord 0.65 × wing root chord (GA ratios, assumed)
Ultimate tail load 0.12 × MTOW·g·n_ult, elliptic spanwise (assumed balance + manoeuvre load)
Torque from load at c/4 about the 0.35c box reference; webs at 12% and 65% chord
Uniform-gauge baseline from a first-pass hand sizing to margin +0.25; skin buckling not checked
horizontal_tail.convergence_note: Peak σ_vM re-solved at three node counts.

fuselage_frames.name: Wing Carry-Through Ring Frames & Bridge
fuselage_frames.model: Closed-ring force method (2 redundants, 721 points/half ring) + carry-through beam
assumptions: Fuselage radius 0.64 m scaled from a 1.22 m GA cabin by MTOW^(1/3) (assumed)
Wing root shear split 70% main / 15% front / 15% rear frame; reacted by skin shear q = 2V·sinφ/(πR)
Bridge = spar root I-section carrying the full root moment across the cabin
Frames are 65 mm deep I-sections; uniform-gauge baseline from hand sizing to margin +0.25
fuselage_frames.convergence_note: Frame peak (excluding the bridge) vs ring integration points per half ring.

metrics.governing: carry-through bridge cap (root moment)

ai_proposal.rationale: The carry-through bridge cap is right at the 0.10 margin limit (306 MPa), so we hold the main frame gauge steady while trimming the lightly stressed front and rear ring frames (208 MPa).
ai_proposal.verdict: accepted: solver confirms the constraint and a near-optimal objective

ai_proposal.rationale: Transferring gauge from the secondary front and rear rings into the main frame and carry-through bridge reduces the governing root bending stress at equal mass.

main_landing_gear.name: Cantilever Tubular Main Gear Strut
main_landing_gear.model: Curved cantilever tube: 3D small-rotation curvature integration (bending + Saint-Venant torsion), 33 nodes
assumptions: Landing load factor 3.0 limit × 1.5 ultimate, 90% of MTOW on the mains (assumed, FAR 23.473 style)
Spin-up drag 0.25 × vertical reaction applied at the axle; side load not modelled
Spec material (al_2024_t3) used for the strut: steel is not in the verified material table
Tube OD 120 → 86 mm; uniform wall baseline from hand sizing to margin +0.25
sources: Megson 6ed Ch. 16-18 (bending, torsion of closed tubes)
main_landing_gear.convergence_note: Peak σ_vM re-solved at three node counts.

ai_proposal.rationale: Combined bending and Saint-Venant torsion peaks at the hip attachment (margin 0.25) and decays toward the axle, allowing a modest hip wall reduction and larger axle-end taper.

ai_proposal.verdict: rejected: feasible but more than 2% worse than the solver grid optimum (8.17 kg vs 7.56 kg)

ai_proposal.rationale: Tapering the lightly stressed axle-end tube wall allows thickening the governing s = 0.00 m hip attachment wall to increase safety margin without adding mass.

engine_mount.name: Engine Mount Spaceframe Truss
engine_mount.model: Pin-jointed 3D spaceframe: direct stiffness (24 DOF, 14 bars) + Euler buckling per member
assumptions: Engine + propeller mass 0.11 × MTOW at 0.30 m ahead of the ring, inertia n_ult·m·g (assumed)
Ultimate thrust 1.5 × 0.25 × MTOW·g; propeller torque and gyroscopic loads not modelled
Firewall hard points pinned; members pinned-pinned (K = 1) for buckling
Zone factor k scales tube OD and wall by √k (constant D/t); baseline hand-sized to margin +0.25
engine_mount.convergence_note: Exact for a pin-jointed truss (one bar element per member).

metrics.governing: member D4 (buckling)

ai_proposal.rationale: Member D4 Euler buckling in the diagonal/ring group governs at a 0.25 margin, so we slightly trim the diagonal tubes while more substantially reducing the non-buckling longeron tubes.
ai_proposal.verdict: rejected by solver: margin +0.08, mass 1.09 kg breaks the goal constraint

min_mass.rationale: Grid search over 169 solver runs; lightest gauge set holding margin ≥ +0.10. Longeron tubes ×0.90, diagonal & ring tubes ×1.00: mass -0.03 kg, peak σ_vM 130 → 145 MPa, margin +0.25 → +0.21. Governing: member L3 (buckling).

ai_proposal.rationale: Shifting mass from the axial longerons into the diagonal and ring tubes increases the section radius of gyration and area in member D4, raising its Euler buckling margin.
ai_proposal.verdict: rejected by solver: margin +0.08, mass 1.23 kg breaks the goal constraint
